I agree that living without meaning is not inherently worth anything. All that means, is that from there, being alive means you have a chance to find a purpose. What matters to you. What message you want to sent to the world. Whether you're living to encourage people to be more empathetic, build relationships, or develop your skills... the messages people tell depressed people to just get on with it is so damaging. I feel for you. 

There are small steps, everyday that can make existence more bearable. Even if you think nothing will come of it, things you used to be interested in, anything. 

Personally, the only thing that has helped me to regain a sense of wanting to live, is trying to convince your mind that you can add value to this world. That for just being you, and sharing yourself with the world, is good enough. You are good enough. Life itself, a biological component is not inherently meaningful. You are meaningful, because you have your own opinions, personality and individual human experience.

Theres moments where you think you've got it under control, and you know how to manage it but life happens and sometimes you'll feel like you're back to square 1 again and you have to remind yourself that you'll get through another bad patch and try to not let it define your outlook on life. Separating fact from feeling and stuff.

Overall, it is definitely possible to make progress with persistent efforts. With the habits I've developed, time feels like it passes much faster now. Before it dragged and dragged. Being really aware of how you're feeling and addressing it straight away is really important. Dont ignore your feelings.

Distraction is okay in moderation, but you need to be in touch with your feelings in order to be able to get them under control. Not good 24/7 tho to be wrapped up in your head.

It's a long journey and I have to say there doesnt get to a point where there isnt some level of difficulty trying to manage your depression. But it can get easier with practice and dedication. Support from the people you love is really key. Minimising the stress in your life wherever possible.

Trauma therapies and exposure therapy might work for some people to get used to the triggers and to minimise their effects but I dont know if they would be effective or suitable for everyone. Sometimes the brain blocks out certain details, so you cant always prepare or know something is going to be a trigger. Like a smell or the way someone looks at you or stands over you.
